Phase 56 impl @ db61782 (branch phase/review-bench), per the approved plan docs/phases/review-bench.md.

What changed / where:
- tagteam/snapshots.py (new): temp-index snapshot (read-tree HEAD, add -A, write-tree, commit-tree -p HEAD) + update-ref refs/tagteam/snapshots/P/T/rN/<entry-ts>; row keyed by lead entry ts; base_sha = cycle baseline.sha else HEAD; failures → one stderr note + snapshot_failed diagnostic, never raises.
- tagteam/cycle.py: _capture_snapshot after cycle init and after lead SUBMIT_FOR_REVIEW / AMEND in cycle add (before the on-submit gate).
- tagteam/db.py: schema v11 (submission_snapshots, bench_results) + helpers.
- tagteam/bench.py (new) + tagteam/data/bench/contract.md: select / run (dry run unless --yes, --max-turns 12, resume identity incl. version_ts + provenance + commit + base) / table (per provenance; agree, missed-RC, extra-RC, blk/maj per RC, tokens, seconds; not-ground-truth line). Replay repo = fresh git init in system temp (base → submitted via git archive), outcome scrub of all six cycle copies in both trees before commit, child env TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY=1 + TAGTEAM_BENCH=1, --add-dir for the verdict dir, usage kind=bench with null phase/target.
- cli.py: bench dispatch + help; bench added to READ_ONLY_REFUSED (the classification test requires every dispatched command be listed; behaviour is the plan's 'refused like any unlisted command'). pyproject data/bench/*.md; README, docs/workflows.md, tagteam/data/workflows.md.
- tests/test_snapshots.py (6), tests/test_bench.py (21); test_db v10 assertion relaxed to >= 10.

Verification: focused files while working (test_bench, test_snapshots, test_readonly, test_cycle*, test_gatekeeper, test_controls, test_db, test_report, test_usage, test_project_root: all pass). Full suite: see gate entry @ db61782. Manual on this repo: bench select lists 170 benchable rounds (all provenance none, as expected); a dry run printed grid + '≈ 4 × 1.1M input tokens (proxy…)' and spawned nothing; a real replay repo for measure-the-loop:impl:3@d12ff96..88521a4 had history submitted/base, clean status, correct name-status list, and the target JSONL ending at the gate entry before the verdict. Snapshot capture wall time here: 0.14–0.29 s. No real model cell has been run (that is the post-merge 6x2 measurement).

GATE: PASS | scope 13 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (1971 passed, 5 skipped, 5m28s)
checked: HEAD db61782

REQUEST_CHANGES — reviewed db61782 against the approved plan. Gate result accepted: 1971 passed, 5 skipped. Focused reviewer run: tests/test_bench.py + tests/test_snapshots.py, 27 passed in 10.53s; no full-suite rerun and no real model calls.

1. [major] Give every pair attempt a fresh artifact directory (tagteam/bench.py:570-574, run_command run_id generation). The directory includes round/provenance/cell but omits commit, base and version, while those distinguish valid pairs. Two asserted revisions of the same round/cell in one invocation overwrite the same logs and reuse verdict.json. Reproduced with two Pair objects differing in commit_sha and the same run_id: the first mocked child writes APPROVE, the second writes no verdict, and the second is nevertheless recorded as ok/APPROVE. Second-resolution run IDs also permit collisions across invocations. Use unique run and attempt identities, prevent stale verdict reuse, and deduplicate identical requested pairs before budgeting/spawning. Add a two-revision regression where the second child writes no verdict and must fail.

2. [major] Cleanup must distinguish stale directories from live and explicitly kept ones (tagteam/bench.py:474-479, 575-576). prune_stale_replays deletes every matching project marker; it records/checks neither ownership liveness nor --keep. Starting another bench therefore deletes an active child's cwd, and the next run silently deletes repositories promised by --keep. Reproduced: a newly created owner-marked replay directory is immediately removed. Record/check active ownership and retention, or serialize runs with a lock and retain kept directories; only reclaim provably abandoned, non-kept attempts. Test active, kept and abandoned cases separately.

3. [major] Preserve Git tree contents when materializing replay repositories (tagteam/bench.py:399-405). git archive applies export-ignore/export-subst attributes, so it is not a faithful tree export. Reproduced in a temporary repository: tracked app.py with an 'app.py export-ignore' attribute exists in the source commit but is absent from _extract output. This can remove the very code/tests being reviewed while provenance remains snapshot. Materialize blobs/modes without archive transformations (and avoid applying clean filters again when constructing replay commits), or explicitly refuse unsupported transformations instead of reporting an exact replay. Add tracked export-ignore and export-subst fixtures and compare replay contents outside the intentional scrub paths with the submitted tree.

4. [major] Aggregate latest successful results per reviewed round/version, as the plan specifies (tagteam/bench.py:table_data, latest_ok keyed by _result_identity). The resume identity includes commit/base and is correctly more specific, but reusing it for table aggregation counts multiple asserted tree choices for one round/version as multiple rounds, biasing agreement and token averages toward rounds retried with different revisions. Use a separate aggregation key including phase/type/round/version/provenance/cell; pick the latest ok row within the --run filter. Keep the full identity for resumption. Test two successful asserted revisions for one round/version: table rounds must be 1 and use the latest row.

Temporary reproductions made no project source edits. The arbiter's agreement-only scope, separate asserted provenance and initial 6x2 budget are unchanged.
